title: Etekcity Food Kitchen Scale, Digital Grams and Ounces for Weight Loss, Baking, Cooking, Keto and Meal Prep, LCD Display, Medium, 304 Stainless Steel
description:
About this item
𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗪𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴: Supports 5 units (oz/lb:oz/fl'oz/g/mL), tare function, and includes 2 AAA batteries for hassle-free operation
𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘀: Accurately weighs up to 11 lb/5 kg with 1 g increments
𝗦𝗶𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲 & 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗰𝘁: The small and sleek scale is a perfect fit for most kitchens, occupying little space and easily storable in cabinets
𝗘𝗮𝘀𝘆 𝘁𝗼 𝗖𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻: Just wipe down the 304 food-grade stainless steel surfaces to keep clean
𝗟𝗖𝗗 𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗽𝗹𝗮𝘆: Backlit LCD screen with large fonts for easy reading
reviews_5s:
So Much More than a Kitchen Scale - A "Nutrition" Scale.
I bought this scale - not to lose weight...although it could be used for that - quite effectively, but to track my Sodium, Calories, Fats, Sugars and overall Daily "LIMITS" levels from the Food I consume.
Nothing could work better. ALL the Nutrition DATA is on EVERY product LABEL...from Calories..ALL the way down to mcg. of Vitamins...Potassium..Fiber..etc. the "Killer App" of this scale is that you can SCAN the UPC..."price code" and say 90+% of the time, the EXACT product is found, and uploaded. From then on...take a week to upload your "repeat" food, and anything you add to your diet. If a product is NOT FOUND..you can "create food" and add the nutrition numbers in...it's easy. You can even load a "Taco Bell" Burrito...the nutrition facts are online...easy to find.
Ok...Things to note:
- You have to "ADD" products to get them in the database...BUT they are easy to DELETE...they say 'swipe right or left" Iphone or Android...but do this instead..."PUSH DOWN" on item...gives you delete.
- You can Also add "MEALS"...just make a list of a meal you eat, and click on ... and "Add as a meal"...name it..and it becomes a choice...like a potato.
- You can add grams, oz, ml. etc of food 2 ways..
A. Just tare a bowl..weigh food, enter weight..
B. "LIVE" weight....choose a food from your list...with scale ON...and weight/cal..ALL categories "fill in"...save..and it's recorded. Cool Feature Really.
- You can search food by typing it in - search database (if not in your data)..or it searches your food so no scrolling.
- Sort alphabetically or by "recent" most used..- bummer it doesn't keep your last search criteria.
- You can add your age..height weight gender AND DIET you choose...I did DASH..and it gives you Kcal per day...Calories...
- BUT..you can go to SETTINGS..and enter your Calorie limit/goal...AND Add limits to EACH category...- ie..I put in the LIMITS daily for DASH...2300 mg SODIUM...Down to 15 mcg Vitamin D..
- Given all this...You can..And I do..MEET ALL your limits per day by entering Breakfast lunch dinner snacks...and as the day goes on..you can "customize" dinner..snacks etc. if you are going to go over a limit. (The one exception is SUGARS..I think this scale counts FRUIT sugars equal to added sugars in processed food IMHO)...watch for that.
- Lastly...NUTRITION INFORMATION gives you a rundown of numbers vs limits...and some verbiage on what to do if you blow a limit....green is good..red is over.
- Lastly lastly...lll 3 bars gives you daily, weekly, monthly histograms of calories per meal, and Carbs protein fats per day week month breakdown.
It's entirely possible to enter EVERYTHING you Eat...but it takes a bit of time commitment. Even if you don't enter everything...or skip days...using it a few times correctly gives you an idea of what you are eating "Numerically".
Great product...sturdy..sleek..easy to use...Get One. I bought one for each of my kids.
Customer Cool 4/26/2025When a friend told me about this I thought it was straight out of star trek. "What do you mean you can just put food on a scale and it will tell you what's in it?" I didn't believe it existed until I saw it. I'm used to the manual calculations and all that tedious stuff that makes tracking macros/calories pretty annoying. I get this thing and it just blows my mind. I scan the barcode, weigh the thing, and even better yet they have an app it all plugs into.

Totally redefining how I approach food (a single serving of granola is how small?!) and it's even better when I have to fit in specific macros by the end of the day to meet my goals. You can weigh it with various units, tare it as you add ingredients to get specific measurements. Measurements seem accurate, I'm in a deficit and I'm losing weight so that means the scale is working! Bluetooth is easy, but if you're in a household with more than one person using this scale, sometimes you need to power it off and back on while youre trying to connect to ensure it's your phone that is the one connecting.

Overall, this thing is magic, helping me achieve my goals and I am not kidding when I say this should be in every household, just like every car has a seatbelt. So many people would live healthier lives if they had something this easy to calculate what they're eating each day.

My only fear is that they will put the app behind a subscription, because this scale is all about reducing barriers and doing so would be antithetical to what this scale does.I purchased the Etekcity Food Kitchen Scale to help me accurately measure food portions as part of a New Year's diet. Trying to eyeball portion sizes can be tricky, so using the weight measurements from food labels and this scale makes calorie tracking much more precise.

While I don't have another scale to verify its accuracy, the weight measurements seem consistent and reliable for my needs. The scale is incredibly easy to operate with a single button for on/off and a dedicated tare function that works almost instantly.

Cleaning is a breeze thanks to the stainless steel surface – it simply wipes clean. The LCD display is clear and easy to read. My only minor wish is that it was extendable, as large bowls can sometimes obstruct the view. However, for such an affordable, entry-level scale, this is a minor inconvenience, and you can find models with that feature for a slightly higher price if it's a necessity.

I appreciate the automatic shut-off feature, which prevents accidental battery drain if I forget to turn it off after use. This is my first dedicated kitchen scale, so I don't have a comparison point, but I can say that this Etekcity scale does exactly what I need it to do. It provides accurate weights for my food portions and was very reasonably priced. It's a basic but effective tool that perfectly fulfills its purpose for my dietary needs.Honestly i bought this scale to make macro tracking easier but it's really not. This is a great idea but to get it to work you have to download the app and enter the food anyway. The app was easy to connect and use, but it's another step and does not have a barcode reader. So if you are considering this as an quick step for adding meals to a third party app like MFP, then you're better off using the voice in feature in their app.

That said i like the larger size for plates and the ease of weighing. The scale is easy to read and holds your values without timing out on you. This allows you to tare a plate or bowl and then take it to the stove and fill it without it timekeeping out and losing the tare value.
This has saved me the double plate method a time or two already. It's water resistant and easy to clean. And the design does not really allow for nuts of food to get in beneath the base and scale plate with can cause invalid measurements.
Overall I'm not impressed with the app part but I'm enjoying the scale. This might be differ if i used a tablet in my kitchen, but i generally operate with my android phone.I follow a content creator who does all of his recipes in grams using a food scale. I love his recipes but couldn't really follow the measurements so I ended up buying this scale. I had no idea I would use it as much as I have! I rarely use measuring cups anymore. It saves a step in washing to go straight to the mixing bowl. My husband recently had surgery and wasn't supposed to lift more than 5 lbs. He went to grab the tea out of the fridge and I stopped him because I thought it was too heavy. Thanks to the scale I was able to find out it was 4.6 pounds. It is extremely accurate. I have tested it against liquid measuring cups as well as dry ones and it is perfectly aligned with them. I have bought other things by this company and have found them to be very reliable.I originally found this brand because of the scale to weigh myself! Which I absolutely love! So I already had the app and knew I wanted to try and find the scale through the app on Amazon before purchasing on their website. I knew I wanted to stick with their product because I know their stuff is extremely accurate! With that being said, time to talk about the actual food scale!

I started a weight loss journey a couple days ago. I’ve tried before but I never got serious about it. I’d try working out and a diet but would fail after 5 days. This time I’ve come into it with the best mindset. So when I knew I wanted to do portion control, I wanted to get a scale to help me fully understand the amount of calories I’m in taking every day because the whole calorie thing never made sense to me and it was hard to track using a pen and paper. I’m still trying to learn more about the other things beside calories which I’m hoping with the help of the scale, I’ll be able to do that. But I don’t want to get consumed by counting my calories so i thought, okay let’s get a scale to do it for me! So I went with this one!

First glance, the quality of the product is absolutely amazing! It comes with battery which I was completely shocked by. It’s made well! I love the size and I’m so excited to fully get to use it. I had a mini slim Jim next to me so I went ahead and tested it out using that and it did give me different numbers than the box, but i genuinely believe the scale more than the box. I’ve seen multiple people say the box gives bigger numbers than actual what’s in the product. It’s worth every penny! I highly recommend this product or any of products by this brand if you to are on your weight loss journey and looking for an accurate food scale and I regular scale!The Etekcity Food Kitchen Scale is ideal for helping you measure portion sizes—excellent if you're on a diet. It's easy to use and lightweight, with a single on/off button and tare function. It also has an automatic shutoff, which is a welcome addition. It's reasonably priced and offers a good value for money. It's very easy to clean because its stainless steel surface is water-resistant, and it has an LED display that's very easy to read.We bought this scale for food portion control to help with a diet we are on. My wife loves it. Very accurate, well built, easy to use and cleaning is a snap. It works in conjunction with the app for our diet as well. We've had it for a little while now, and it seems like it will last us for many years to come. Would recommend it to anyone that needs a good scale.It works Really Well, I am on a weigh loss Journey and I definitely recommend, I’ve been using it for a couple of days now and it is straight forward. After you download the app and connect it to Bluetooth you will be good to go. It also has a scanner so no having to type in anything so far. You can easily clean it and it is lightweight, easy to maneuver.I love this scale. I don’t use the app that comes with it but I do use it daily to weigh out portion sizes. Easy to clean. I will say the features on the app are pretty cool as well but I just don’t use it in that way. But if you really wanted an accurate macro count I’d use the app. It’s easy to switch between measurements and easy to clean.
reviews_1s:
I purchased this scale and to say I regret it would be an understatement. I did not find any value in the features that you see advertised. I honestly thought the food database would be better or at least exist for most foods.

1. You have to scan or manually enter everything. I have not found 1 food it has in its database already.
2. All the videos you see where it’s showing the nutritional information, that’s after you scan or input it.
3. There is no option to delete an item.
4. The only options once an item is created is to modify it as in change the nutritional info and move it to a different day.
So if you add the wrong thing to you meal, oh well.
5. Uninstalling and reinstalling app doesn’t reset anything you added. Deleting the scale and adding it back also doesn’t
remove anything once add.
6. The info even when you scan the barcode is a little off. I found calorie, carbs, fat and sodium were all off by a little.
7. The scale will turn off after 2 minutes. No, it’s not hard to turn back on, but you don’t have and option to set for more
than 2 minutes.
8. Check your privacy settings. Everything is on as in data they can capture/you signed up for promotional info.
Got to love the auto sign up for the User Experience Program.
9. Too many built in add-ons like scenes, roo you can manage, etc. All you wanted was a scale and you have ads others
items that are sold.
10. There is a forum section where other people who have any device use this app have posted questions. Again, just
wanted a scale that could give me nutritional information..
Ironically I found the question how to delete a food item, no response back.Some people will use the scale over a couple mines , watching weight as they add things. For example, when making a coffee pour over, you might add 15 grams of beans to your vessel, and then add perhaps 240 grams of water second. And then some techniques have you add some water, then weight a bit before adding the rest - up to 240 gram mark.

The HUGE problem here is that the scale turns off frequently, and there is no way to wake it up - to simple resume and show the present weight. Instead. every press of the combined on/tare bottom resets the scale to zero.

When making coffee like above, you might have just added 128 grams of water, and it turns off. When you click the button to "wake it", it reads zero. So how far away are you from your goal of 240 grams? There is no way to tell. You're done.

If you're lucky - you might have glanced at the scale before it turned off - and saw maybe 122 grams. Then you can do some arithmetic in your head and figure out that you need to add - whatever- more... But most of the time, I glance down - and see the blank screen. and have the guess.

I didn't buy a scale so I could guess weights, and even worse, I shouldn't be worrying about the thing sabotaging me when trying to make a nice relaxing cup of coffee.I can’t believe this wasn’t mentioned more in reviews. This scale is agonizingly slow to measure., and it’s always off by 2+ grams.

I got this to replace a 20 year old Sharper Image kitchen scale that still works, but occasionally freezes up, requiring you to dump your ingredient and start all over. Frustrating!

So I found this, solid reviews, and it looks great. I reallly wanted it usb c rechargeable, not those stupid AA batteries that always explode and corrode your gear. And yes, the design, build quality, and overall feel of this scale, and the controls on it, are very well done. Great! And it’s USB-C! Man I really wanted to like this.

Excitedly, I began weighing out dinner for our pups. And I kid you not, I had to weight the same bowl about 8 times. This scale is sooo slow to update, that I’d think I hit the desired weight, be all set to move the bowl, and then suddenly I’m 12 grams over! It’s a good thing I used my sharper image scale to compare the weights!

This scale consistently weighed heavy, unless I sat for 10-20 seconds EACH TIME I added some kibble, to let the unit update the weight. Even then it was off by 2-3 grams always.

I guess if you don’t care about accurately measuring your ingredients, get this? I thought that was the entire point of a food scale. Forgot about weighing espresso or anything else that requires precision.

My old sharper image updates the display with the weight damn near instantly, reacting well with each kibble I add to the bowl. It measures espresso and spices to the tenth decimal with perfect accuracy. That is what a kitchen scale should do.

This thing drove me mad with two uses. Cannot recommend it. It’s accurate, but you’re gonna mess up your measurements unless you have the patience of a saint and the time of a retired travel agent.

Easy pass, don’t buy. I’m requesting a refund and looking for another brand.**Update 5/26/25**
I hate this scale so much. The sensitivity is total garbage and doesn’t detect small changes in weight. I added a photo of me adding almond butter that was almost empty so it was dripping very slowly into the container. I had added at least 10-15g and it still said 0g. It will also change without adding/removing things. Maybe I got a lemon but I would not rebuy this scale nor recommend it.

I love the look and design of this scale. It was pretty much exactly what I was looking for. The rechargeable function is awesome too because I hate replacing batteries. It’s also very easy to clean.

However my biggest gripe with this scale is that it is not very sensitive, especially if you are weighing in grams. It won’t detect slight changes until you’ve gone over the desired weight, then you have to remove product. It’s kinda frustrating if you’re at all OCD like me and have to have things perfect. I’ve found if I get the scale like a gram or two under and then add some pressure to get it to recalculate, it will adjust and be at the weight I want. Kinda a dumb issue when weighing things accurately is the whole point of a scale.Bought 3months ago and it does not weigh accurately whatsoever! I used it the first week and it was working fine -have not used again till last week and it’s completely inaccurate! I changed the batteries thinking maybe that would fix it but NO! I can put a pound on it and it shows the weight as 9 ounces and if I move the weight over an inch it says it weighs 4 ounces I’ve tested it over and over What a waste of money!Not sure how I'm feeling about this scale. I have a similar food scale that I thought was the same model, but the old one I have works a lot better. This new one has two primary problems:

1. The display darkens after a while of no change in weight, making it really difficult to see the measurement. So difficult, in fact, that you may make the assumption that the scale has completely turned itself off. This causes problems because you end up removing the item that you're weighing, which resets the weight, just to find the display comes back on again after being jostled. Not sure if this is intended behavior but it's annoying.

2. The weight changes when nothing is interacting with the scale. I put some water on the scale at 230 g, and then ~15 seconds later it was 229 g. A few seconds after that, it was 228 g. I let it sit there and the scale eventually made its way down to 225 g after about a minute. What is even happening with this thing?

I like the form factor and ease of use, but really I can't recommend this scale.I brought this scale and thought it replace the other Etekcity scale I had years ago because my old one stopped working. It wouldn't turn on. So I opted in for a cheaper slimmer one of their brand. However I have to say the scale is just off. I will set the scale to zero and measure in grams for all baking needs. I mainly bake breads so precise measurement would make things easier. The problem is if I weight some the first time, its accurate but the scale does wonky. For example lets say I need 40 grams of honey and I over pour to 50 grams. Then I want just scoop up some of the honey back to equal 40 grams. This will not happen... as I scoop the honey back, you would think it goes down in grams but instead it over weight. It went up to like 65 grams? We are removing honey right? so it should be less! but it acts all wonky for reason. I have tried this several items even flour sugar etc and it does the same thing.

Oh if you remove an empty plate or bowl after you already tare it and put it back down, it should reset it to zero. I tested this many times and it never does that it starts weight things with nothing on it... this should not happen. I feel I should just return the scale. While its probably ok if you need approx weight for food. It's not ok if you are baking with precision. Just annoying to deal with to tarte so many times even if you haven't added anything new in the bowl.I had high hopes for this smart scale, but it has been nothing short of a frustrating experience. The marketing makes it sound revolutionary, but in reality, it’s plagued by bugs and poorly thought-out functionality.

First, the food database is incredibly limited when it comes to measurements in grams. Many common foods aren’t included, making it difficult to get accurate macro readings. This issue completely undermines the purpose of the product.

Second, using this scale to plan or calorie count meals is a headache. It’s barely more convenient than setting up your own spreadsheet and using a reliable calorie-tracking app. In fact, I’ve found it faster and more accurate to just use other tools.

Third, the scale doesn’t allow you to create your own meals, measure portions in grams, and get macro breakdowns for those meals. For anyone trying to batch cook or portion out meals, this is a glaring oversight.

Overall, this product feels half-baked and overpriced for what it offers. Save your money and invest in a basic kitchen scale and a good calorie-tracking app instead.
